claims.text: A CPA-based simulation incorporating disorder and local relaxations will predict the electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than conventional analytical methods.
The proposed accuracy advantage will apply in both the approximately 0–200 K and 300–1200 K temperature regimes.
The proposed method will be particularly advantageous for HfNbTaTiZr samples containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Conventional analytical methods for this problem assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
The proposed CPA-based method incorporates atomic disorder and local lattice relaxations associated with intrinsic compositional complexity and oxygen impurities.
Experimental conductivity measurements are available or will be conducted for HfNbTaTiZr samples with and without 1 wt.% oxygen over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The multicomponent alloy structure produces atomic-scale disorder and local lattice distortions.
Oxygen impurities produce additional local lattice distortions or defects in HfNbTaTiZr.
Atomic disorder and local relaxations affect conductivity through electron scattering and other non-ideal effects.
Representing disorder-driven scattering and non-ideal effects will improve conductivity-prediction accuracy relative to perfect-crystal models.
The CPA-based conductivity curves will agree more closely with experimental measurements across the specified temperature ranges.
The predicted conductivity trends will systematically reflect the presence of 1 wt.% oxygen.
Perfect-crystal analytical models are less sensitive to local-disorder effects than the proposed simulation.
The expected accuracy advantage is limited to bulk samples with roughly the stated oxygen level and to 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The approach may not extend to substantially different impurity levels or temperatures outside the specified ranges.
